faqs.question: What do you write in a Halloween card?
faqs.answer: Write their name, one memory only the two of you share, and a warm sign-off. Two or three lines is enough; the memory is what makes it worth keeping. If you are stuck, start with "Halloween always reminds me of…" and finish the sentence honestly.

faqs.question: What is a good short Halloween greeting for a text?
faqs.answer: Keep it under about 20 words so it reads in a notification preview, for example "Boo. That's the whole text." or "Happy Halloween! Costume photo or it didn't happen." On SubhSandesh, 48.3% of all page views happen on a phone, so short wins.

faqs.question: Is it OK to wish someone happy Halloween if they don't celebrate it?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you drop the spooky part. Send something like "Wishing you a restful evening, whatever you're celebrating or skipping" and do not push the holiday itself.

faqs.question: What should I say to coworkers on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Keep it light, inclusive and non-romantic: "Happy Halloween, team. Quiet inboxes and full snack drawers to all." Avoid anything about dating or scares aimed at one person, and never send a "Will you be my boo?" page to a colleague.

faqs.question: What time should I send a Halloween message to family in another country?
faqs.answer: Send for their evening, not yours. 7 p.m. on 31 October in New York is already 4:30 a.m. on 1 November in India and 10 a.m. on 1 November in Sydney, so wishes to Asia or Australia should go out during your morning.

faqs.question: When is Halloween every year?
faqs.answer: Halloween is always 31 October. It falls on a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027, followed by All Saints' Day on 1 November.

faqs.question: How do you sign off an email on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Swap your usual closing for a one-line seasonal one, such as "Have a happy, not-too-haunted Halloween," or "Boo, and best regards,". Keep it to the last email of 30 or 31 October so it doesn't feel forced.

faqs.question: How long should a Halloween voice note be?
faqs.answer: About 15 to 20 seconds: their name, one specific thing that made you think of them, and happy Halloween. Longer voice notes tend to get saved for later rather than played.

faqs.question: Are funny Halloween wishes better than sweet ones?
faqs.answer: Match the person, not the holiday. A pun works for a best friend; a grandparent or someone far away usually values one real memory more than a joke.

faqs.question: Can I send a Halloween wish as an interactive page instead of a text?
faqs.answer: Yes. SubhSandesh's Halloween page lets the recipient knock on a haunted house, carve a pumpkin with your word and read your letter by flashlight, with partner, bestie, family and kids modes. It is meant for one person, not a group, and its interface is English only.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Happy Halloween Wishes: 66 Original Lines by Person and Channel

The best happy Halloween wish fits in two lines: their name, one thing only you two share, and a sign-off that suits the channel. Below are 66 original happy Halloween wishes, sorted by recipient and by channel, plus a three-part formula and 31 October timing across time zones.

Keep them short: across all SubhSandesh pages, 48.3% of views happen on a phone. People also reread messages they like: the average page here is viewed 11.1 times, so the specific memory matters more than the pun. Both figures are platform-wide, not Halloween data.

## What is a Halloween wish, and how is it different from a card message?

A Halloween wish is a short, warm message sent on or just before 31 October to one person or household. A card message is the same wish, longer and handwritten.

In a 2024 study of golden-age Halloween postcards (about 1900 to 1920), [Adrienne Darrah of Penn State](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jacc.13580) notes a postcard cost 1¢ to buy and 1¢ to mail, against 3¢ to post a greeting card, and that US postcard sales passed one billion by 1909. Postcards had no envelope, so every line was public.

## 42 Halloween wishes by recipient

Swap the brackets for your own details. Six lines per person.

### For your partner

- You're the only person I'd split my last caramel apple with. Happy Halloween.
- You're my favourite thing about October, and October has pumpkins.
- You pick the scariest film, I hide behind you. Same plan tonight?
- Happy Halloween to my partner in crime and in badly matched costumes.
- I'd still choose you over a full bag of candy. Mostly.
- Tonight's forecast: one blanket, two of us, every light off. Happy Halloween, boo.

### For your best friend

- You have photos of every costume mistake I've made. Happy Halloween, keep them hidden.
- We've been haunting each other since [year]. Happy Halloween, bestie.
- If a ghost shows up, I'm calling you first. Then running.
- Still sorry about the [party] disaster. This candy is my apology.
- Friends who scream at the same jump scares stay friends.
- My Halloween plan: whatever you're doing, but louder.

### For family

- Mum and Dad, thank you for every costume stitched at midnight.
- To my sister, who still hides behind doors: I'm ready this time.
- To the family that turns 31 October into a group project.
- Grandma, your pumpkin soup is still the best part of Halloween.
- From our house to yours: may the candy last.
- Happy Halloween, little brother. You're still banned from handing out raisins.

### For a coworker

- Happy Halloween, team. Quiet inboxes and full snack drawers to all.
- Wishing you fewer spreadsheets and more chocolate this Halloween.
- You make Mondays less frightening than any haunted house.
- Leave the ghosts at reception and grab a cupcake from the kitchen.
- To the colleague who makes Friday deadlines survivable: happy Halloween.
- Wishing you a calm, candy-filled evening.

### For a neighbour

- Happy Halloween from number [12]! Porch light on, bowl full.
- Thanks for being the house every kid on our street loves.
- If our pumpkin ends up on your step, blame the wind.
- Wishing your family a safe, sweet Halloween night.
- We left a few treats by your door. Happy Halloween from next door.
- Knock if you run out of candy; we over-bought again.

### For someone far away

- It's night here and morning there, so happy Halloween for your tonight.
- Carving a pumpkin without you felt wrong, so I gave it your grin.
- Miles apart, same October moon. Happy Halloween from here.
- I saved you a fun-size bar. It'll be stale by then.
- Call me once your trick-or-treaters are done; I'll be up.
- Our old street is lit up and I thought of you at every door.

### For someone who doesn't celebrate Halloween

Some skip it for religious or personal reasons. Drop the ghosts, keep the warmth.

- No costume needed: wishing you a cosy evening and a good end to October.
- I know Halloween isn't your thing, so simply: thinking of you today.
- Happy end of October! Hope your evening is quiet and your tea is hot.
- Skipping the spooky part, sending the warm part: I'm glad you're in my life.
- Wishing you a restful evening, whatever you're celebrating or skipping.
- Here's to 1 November and a calm, fresh month.

Dedicated guides cover Halloween messages for kids, messages for adults, wishes for grandchildren, Instagram wishes, WhatsApp status lines and romantic quotes. This page is the hub for everyone else.

## 24 Halloween wishes by channel: card, text, email and voice note

A card has room for a memory; a text should fit a notification preview; an email sign-off is one line; a voice note runs 15 to 20 seconds. Cards have long mixed the macabre with the merry. Theatre historian [Matthew McMahan wrote in The Conversation (22 December 2020)](https://theconversation.com/how-holiday-cards-help-us-cope-with-a-not-so-merry-year-according-to-a-professor-of-comedy-152382) that the first Christmas card, usually credited to Henry Cole, was a run of 1,000 in 1843, and that joke cards record how people really feel.

### Halloween card messages

- Dear [name], Halloween always means [memory]. Hope tonight brings a new one.
- To my best trick-or-treat partner: the bags got smaller, the friendship didn't.
- Inside: zero ghosts, one hug, and a reminder that you're loved.
- For [name], who makes every season less scary. Love from all of us.
- Thank you for [specific thing] this year. It meant a lot.
- May your pumpkin glow and your porch stay egg-free.

### Halloween texts to send

- Happy Halloween! Costume photo or it didn't happen.
- Boo. That's the whole text.
- Eat one for me, the good kind, not the raisins.
- Thinking of you and our [year] costume. Happy Halloween!
- Spooky check-in: hiding from trick-or-treaters, or giving full-size bars?
- Who's finishing the candy corn this year, you or the bin?

### Halloween email sign-offs

- Have a happy, not-too-haunted Halloween,
- Wishing you a treat-filled evening,
- Signing off before the ghosts clock in,
- Boo, and best regards,
- Hope your 31 October is all treats,
- Spooky regards from [team],

### Halloween voice-note scripts

- "Hi [name], just passed a giant skeleton and thought of you. Happy Halloween!"
- "Knock knock. No costume, just my voice saying happy Halloween."
- "Halloween report: [dog] went as [costume], candy stolen, one pumpkin collapsed."
- "It's morning there, I know. I wanted you to hear happy Halloween."
- "Happy Halloween, Gran. We carved your pattern again: still a surprised cat."
- "Costume photo within the hour, [name], or I tell everyone about [year]."

## How to write your own Halloween wish in 3 parts

Name, one specific memory, sign-off. The memory does the work.

In a [randomised experiment with 958 Australian adults (Regan, Walsh and Lyubomirsky, Affective Science, 2023)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10104980), people who wrote gratitude letters to particular individuals reported stronger gratitude and positive emotion than list-writers, and the lists did no better than a control task. It measured the writer, not the recipient, but the direction is clear: specific beats generic.

**Worked example 1, best friend:**

- Greeting: "Happy Halloween, Priya!"
- Memory: "Still laughing that we went as salt and pepper and everyone guessed ketchup."
- Sign-off: "Same time next year? Sam."

**Worked example 2, a dad far away:**

- Greeting: "Happy Halloween, Dad."
- Memory: "Mum sent me your wonky-eyebrow pumpkin. It's my lock screen now."
- Sign-off: "Talk Sunday. Love, Aisha."

## When to send Halloween wishes: 31 October and time zones

Halloween is 31 October every year: a Saturday in 2026, a Sunday in 2027. Text in the late afternoon; post cards to arrive by 30 October.

For family abroad, send for their evening. Per the [IANA time zone database](https://www.iana.org/time-zones), 7 p.m. on 31 October in New York is 11 p.m. in London, 4:30 a.m. on 1 November in India and 10 a.m. on 1 November in Sydney, in 2026 and 2027. UK clocks go back on 25 October 2026, and on Halloween morning itself in 2027.

Most people leave it late: in our nearest analogue, Raksha Bandhan 2026, 49.4% of 89 pages were built on the day itself. That is a small, non-Halloween sample.

| Channel | Good length | When to send | SubhSandesh measurement (platform-wide) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text | 5–20 words | 4–6 p.m. their time | 48.3% of page views are on a phone |
| Voice note | 15–20 seconds | Their early evening | Not measured |
| Card | 25–60 words | Arrives by 30 October | Not measurable offline |
| Interactive page | Letter plus up to 6 photos | Link sent by their evening | 11.1 average views per page; 90.9% of started pages published |

Texts win on speed. Only the page row has a measured reread figure.

## A Halloween wish that is a whole page

When two lines feel too small, the [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) turns a wish into a little haunted house. Add both names, a letter, up to six photos and a word to carve, or let the AI write it from a description. They knock three times, carve a jack-o'-lantern until your word glows, wipe fog off portraits to find your photos, read your letter by flashlight and brew a potion from three to five memories.

Partner, bestie, family or kids mode changes the closing question; the default "Will you be my boo?" is editable up to 60 characters, and you get an email when they first answer. For another time zone, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds an optional unlock time, showing only their name and a countdown until then, plus a voice note up to 60 seconds. Both end with a downloadable Boo License.

## When a short wish beats a Halloween page

A page is a one-person greeting, not a party invitation or office broadcast. For coworkers, neighbours or group chats, send a line from above; "Will you be my boo?" is wrong for your manager.

The interface is English only, and 48.3% of views come from phones. For a grandparent who never opens links, a card wins.

## Sources

- Darrah, A. Golden age Halloween postcards. *Journal of American Culture*, 15 August 2024. [Wiley](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jacc.13580)
- Regan, Walsh and Lyubomirsky. Expressing gratitude, randomized experiment. *Affective Science*, 2023. [Europe PMC](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10104980)
- McMahan, M. How holiday cards help us cope. *The Conversation*, 22 December 2020. [Article](https://theconversation.com/how-holiday-cards-help-us-cope-with-a-not-so-merry-year-according-to-a-professor-of-comedy-152382)
- IANA Time Zone Database, continuously updated. [iana.org](https://www.iana.org/time-zones)

Darrah, Journal of American Culture (CC BY-NC-ND). Read via OpenAlex-indexed full text; Wiley page 403.

Date/festival reference (time-zone fact-check, not research): offsets for 31 Oct computed from the tz database — 19:00 New York = 23:00 London = 04:30 1 Nov India = 10:00 1 Nov Sydney in 2026 and 2027; UK clocks go back 25 Oct 2026 and 31 Oct 2027.

structuralLimitations: No Halloween usage data exists in facts.md; every first-party figure is platform-wide and labelled so in the body. The lead-time line is Raksha Bandhan (n=89), disclosed in the body as a non-Halloween analogue.

Darrah 2024 (Wiley) could not be fetched from the publisher (HTTP 403); verified against the full text indexed by OpenAlex. Regan et al. measured the WRITER's wellbeing, not the recipient's; the body says so.
Kumar & Epley 2018 (Psychological Science, SAGE) is banned; the open-access substitute is Regan, Walsh & Lyubomirsky (Affective Science, CC BY, via Europe PMC — exempt host).

IANA is a time-zone fact-check (declared as a date reference), not research. timeanddate.com returned 403; offsets were computed from the tz database via Node Intl and the UK clock-change dates checked the same way.

SERP (Firecrawl, United States): 3 weak results in the top 10 (pinterest x2, facebook) plus 1 off-intent page (Good Housekeeping crafts). Incumbents are card/flower retailers (1800flowers, cardsnacks, myglobalflowers, americangreetings, fnp) and yahoo/parade; none cited. Matches serps.md (weak 3).

Recipient grouping is table stakes (cardsnacks and myglobalflowers both group by relationship); the differentiators are the doesn't-celebrate group, channel groups, voice-note scripts and time-zone timing.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over the five pages analysed for the time-zone timing (no top-5 page gives one), the doesn't-celebrate and voice-note groups, and the gratitude-letter and postcard research that none of them cite; the wishes themselves are original but a list of lines is not, by itself, a moat. It faces card and flower retailers with far more domain authority, and the first-party figures are platform-wide rather than Halloween-specific, which weakens them.
